The memo, which FBI Director Christopher Wray and DOJ officials strongly disputed as misleading and incomplete, was framed by Trump as proving 'total vindication' in the Russia investigation. Democrats released a counter-memo demonstrating that the Nunes memo omitted critical facts, including that the Page surveillance was based on multiple sources and that the FBI had already been investigating Page before the dossier. existing.description_short: Alien Enemies Act Invoked Against Venezuelan Nationals, March 2025
existing.description_long: On March 14, 2025, President Trump signed Proclamation 10903 invoking the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 — last used by FDR during WWII — to declare Tren de Aragua (TdA) a hostile invading force and subject all Venezuelan nationals aged 14 or older who are TdA members to immediate summary deportation without standard immigration proceedings. The State Department had designated TdA a Foreign Terrorist Organization on February 20, 2025. Within hours of the proclamation, the ACLU filed suit and Chief Judge James Boasberg of the D.C. District Court issued a temporary restraining order blocking deportations, verbally ordering flights already in the air to turn around. The administration defied his verbal order, completing deportations anyway; the DOJ argued the written order had not yet been issued when the planes departed. Legal scholars widely criticized the proclamation's framing of immigration as a wartime 'invasion' as a radical distortion of a law written for actual declared wars.

existing.description_short: Trump Fires All Three Election Assistance Commission Members Before Midterms
existing.description_long: On July 9, 2026 — less than four months before the November midterms — President Trump fired all three remaining members of the bipartisan Election Assistance Commission, leaving the federal agency that certifies voting systems, distributes election security grants, and maintains the national voter registration form without any commissioners. Democratic commissioners Thomas Hicks and Benjamin W. Hovland received brief termination emails from White House aide Morgan DeWitt Snow. Republican commissioner Christy McCormick was pressured to resign. A fourth commissioner, Republican Don Palmer, had already resigned in April for a Heritage Foundation post. The White House justified the firings by citing the Supreme Court's June 2026 ruling expanding presidential authority to remove independent agency members. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it a brazen attempt to seize control of our elections before a single vote is cast. With CISA already gutted, the EAC was one of the few remaining federal entities providing election security support to states.

existing.title: Supreme Court Orders Trump to Facilitate Return of Wrongly Deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia
existing.description_short: Supreme Court Orders Trump to Facilitate Return of Wrongly Deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia
existing.description_long: On April 10, 2025, the U.S. Supreme Court — in an 8-1 unsigned order — directed the Trump administration to 'facilitate' the return of Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national who had been living in Maryland with his family and had a court-ordered stay of removal, who was nonetheless deported to El Salvador and sent to the brutal CECOT maximum-security prison in an acknowledged administrative error. The administration had admitted in court that Abrego Garcia's deportation was a mistake. The Supreme Court's rare and rapid intervention underscored the gravity of the situation — a man had been wrongly imprisoned in a foreign torture facility against explicit court orders. The unanimous nature of the order, joined even by justices appointed by Trump, signaled that the Court viewed the administration's conduct as an affront to basic constitutional principles. Legal scholars called the case a test of whether constitutional rights and court orders retained any meaning under the Trump administration.

original_title: Trump Deploys Marines and Federalized National Guard to Los Angeles Over Protests

existing.title: Trump Deploys Marines and Federalized National Guard to Los Angeles Over Protests
existing.description_short: Trump Deploys Marines and Federalized National Guard to Los Angeles Over Protests
existing.description_long: On June 7, 2025, Trump issued a presidential memorandum deploying approximately 2,000 California National Guard troops — taken from Governor Gavin Newsom's control against his explicit objections — plus 700 active-duty Marines to Los Angeles in response to protests against ICE immigration raids. The administration labeled the protests a possible form of rebellion against the authority of the U.S. government. Newsom called the deployment unnecessary and counterproductive. Federal Judge Charles Breyer issued a temporary restraining order on June 12, ruling Trump had failed to meet the legal prerequisites under 10 U.S.C. 12406. A federal judge later ruled the Marines' presence violated the Posse Comitatus Act, which bars the military from domestic law enforcement. The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals partially reversed. The administration deployed up to 4,000 National Guard personnel and relied on legal theories of implied presidential protective power for the Marines. Legal scholars described it as the most aggressive domestic military deployment against civilian protesters in decades.

Trump recorded a promotional video declaring 'I love the Bible. The Bible grift represents Trump’s consistent strategy of harvesting evangelical loyalty as a commercial revenue stream while demonstrating no personal theological literacy or sincerity.

original_title: Iran Nuclear Talks Collapse After Five Rounds

existing.title: Iran Nuclear Talks Collapse After Five Rounds
existing.description_short: Iran Nuclear Talks Collapse After Five Rounds
existing.description_long: From April through May 2025, the Trump administration conducted five rounds of nuclear negotiations with Iran — the first such direct US-Iran diplomatic contact since 2017 — mediated by Oman and held in Muscat and Rome. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff initially floated allowing Iran to enrich uranium at 3.67%, then reversed course demanding total dismantlement of all enrichment capability, which he called a red line. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called enrichment non-negotiable. By the fifth round in Rome on May 23, Oman's mediator reported some but not conclusive progress. Witkoff left early. Iran had accelerated enrichment to 60% purity, enough to produce material for over a dozen weapons within weeks. A bipartisan letter signed by 52 senators and 177 representatives warned Trump against any deal allowing Iran to retain any enrichment capability. Talks formally collapsed when Trump, frustrated with the pace, privately issued ultimatums to Tehran and then ordered military strikes without returning to negotiations, bypassing Congress entirely.
